sentences.text: The only known species is Cratoavis cearensis, a member of the enantiornithines, a diverse group of early birds.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is an articulated skeleton preserved with attached feathers, muscle tissue, and skin traces. It features thinner skeletal structures compared to other enantiornithine birds.
Fish remains found near the intestine of the holotype, the articulated skeleton preserved with attached feathers, muscle tissue, and skin traces, provide direct evidence that Cratoavis ate fish.

The fossil was found in the Early Cretaceous Araripe Basin in Ceará, Brazil. The genus name Cratoavis honors the Crato Formation where the specimen was discovered, while the species name cearensis refers to the state of Ceará.
Cratoavis lived during the Late Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 125.45 and 112.6 million years ago, with the fossil record spanning from 119.57 to 113.2 million years ago.
